shared_elements: frontal standing/upright human or anthropomorphic figure occupying the whole slab
elaborate headdress or head ornament on top
circular disc motif on the torso
belt or waist band with hanging elements
low-relief carving on a tall vertical stone slab
justification: Both depict a single frontal upright anthropomorphic personage filling a tall vertical slab, with a head/headdress at top, chest ornaments including a round disc-like element at the sternum, and a belt-like horizontal band across the waist with pendant elements below. The clearest difference is in execution and detail: A is a densely carved, deeply modelled figure with fully articulated arms, legs, hands and profuse ornament, while B is a highly abbreviated, blocky columnar form with a schematic head and only sparse incised motifs and no depicted limbs.
